gaps.note: Tempo had no network unit in cycle 19, and only theme-tempo-nested-exec touched it, which listed callers of the nested execution path and reran no vector. T14 activates on 8 December 2026 and T15 on 15 December. Tempo runs one client (evm2 with ruint 1.21.1, whose arithmetic paths were rewritten in October 2026), so a fault there is the network's answer and no second client would reject the block. The cycle 18 rerun under a block time override is the only evidence for T14, and nobody has read the evm2 or ruint revision that the T14 release pins.

Eight more networks had no network unit in cycle 19: Ethereum, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Arc and HyperEVM. Only theme units touched them (census, Inbox reading, HyperEVM Algebra swaps), and none reran the battery, the targeted set or script sets 1, 2 and 6 at the current builds. OPCODES.md lists unpublished builds behind the endpoints of Arc, Elysium, Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain, so each new build string since cycle 18 is untested.

established-l1 states in its L-865 result that Celo op-geth c7ed55b8 was not covered by the scan of Go fault shapes. theme-census-endpoints reports from op-geth pull request 509 that op-geth rejected canonical block 75,046,581 and that celo-reth's rule is still live in the sequencer, while F-116 says forno routes a minority of reads to op-geth. If forno's op-geth backend is stalled or diverged, every Celo read result that did not pin the client may come from a node whose state is not canonical. No unit this cycle checked which Celo results were pinned.

L-814 is inconclusive because the Go issue milestones are on GitHub, which this session cannot read. The fix lists of go1.25.6 to go1.25.13 and of the go1.26 releases that bor, BNB Chain geth and avalanchego build with are therefore unread. The Go release history page on go.dev and the go.googlesource.com source mirror were not tried as alternatives.

No unit has examined the multicoin namespace of the C-Chain. coreth core/extstate/statedb.go on master (fetched by the critic from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/coreth/master/core/extstate/statedb.go, lines 92-139) keeps multicoin balances in the same account storage as contract slots: GetBalanceMultiCoin and AddBalanceMultiCoin set bit 0 of byte 0 of the coin id and call GetState and SetState with SkipStateKeyTransformation, and normalizeStateKey clears that bit for every EVM key. That is the reason for the bit 248 fold recorded as F-040. F-040 explains the fold as a client quirk and does not name the namespace it protects or ask who can write into it. plugin/evm/atomic/import_tx.go lines 106-116 reject non-AVAX imports from Banff, and line 346 still credits multicoin balances on the older path.

The theme-hyperevm-algebra verifier asks whether any chain 999 clearance rests on eth_call, eth_getStorageAt or eth_getBalance at a past block sent to https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm. If that endpoint answers past-block queries from latest state, the replay and census results that used it describe the wrong state. No unit has listed the clearances that would be affected.

op-stack-eth measured that eth_call on all seven endpoints grants about 30 million gas, while a mined ordinary transaction is capped at 16,777,216 gas under Karst and Azul. Every simulated script above that cap in OPCODES.md (pmdiff, pmdiff2, the full-range swaps) describes a call no user can mine. The cycle 18 claim that no ordinary account can make a liquidity removal too large for one transaction was measured against the larger simulated limit, not against the cap.

titles: MegaETH skips every remaining candidate of a block once that block holds 1,000 new state entries, so one cheap transaction per block delays PoolManager exits for the rest of the block
One transaction can use the whole per-block budget for new state on MegaETH, and the node skips every later candidate of that block
duplicates.note: high-throughput filed its finding under F-062, but it restates the confirmed base claim of F-042 with a newer build string and file comparison, as its verifier says. Merge the new evidence into F-042 and leave F-062 as the plausible amplified multi-block form.

titles: op-stack-eth profile L2 for all seven chains: No deposit can carry the PoolManager as sender

OP Stack portal upgraders can emit a deposit whose sender is the PoolManager, and op-geth and op-revm run it without nonce or code checks, as OP Mainnet governance did for another address on 2026-10-31
duplicates.note: These read as a contradiction. The op-stack-eth statement holds for ordinary accounts through the deployed portal; theme-inbox-deployed shows that the portal's upgrader can do it. The profile text should say 'no ordinary account' so the ledger does not record the stronger statement.

titles: Under Jenner every address of the CAS20 range answers every call with a revert, and the PoolManager has no funds a pool could hold in such a currency
established-l1 verdict correction: addresses whose byte 10 is 0x02 or 0xff also reverted under the override
duplicates.note: The finding and its verifier disagree with the tagged source. bsc v1.8.2 core/vm/cas20.go resolveCAS20 (lines 122-135) and resolveCAS20Token return no precompile for an ordinal other than 0x00 or 0x01, and core/vm/evm.go lines 46-59 then treat the address as an ordinary account, which answers empty success. The live probe under the Jenner override reverted at byte 10 = 0x02 and 0xff. Either the probe was misread or the dataseed build 4e1c8247 routes differently from the tag (fetched by the critic from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20.go and .../core/vm/evm.go).

leads.question: On the first day T14 is live on Tempo mainnet (8 December 2026), what evm2 commit and ruint version does the T14 release's Cargo.lock pin? Do the battery, the targeted set, the ruint 1.21 vectors and script sets 1, 2 and 6 give the recorded words on the live fork at the real PoolManager address? Repeat both checks for T15 on 15 December.
leads.why: Tempo has one client. A wrong MULMOD, division or shift word in a new interpreter or library release would be the chain's consensus result, and an ordinary account could use it against any pool at once. Only a simulation under a time override covers T14 today.

leads.question: Does Tempo publish or imply the CPU architecture of its validators, for example aarch64 hosts or a release artifact for arm64? If an arm64 build exists, does evm2's jump destination scan choose a NEON or scalar kernel there, and does that kernel give the same JUMPDEST map as the specification on the deployed PoolManager bytecode and on the 442,577 bytecodes cycle 18 used for the x86 kernels?
leads.why: Cycle 18 tested only the three x86 kernels and OPCODES.md lists ruint 1.21.1 on non-x86 targets as open. A validator with a different JUMPDEST map for the PoolManager would reject or accept jumps in pool math differently. On a single-client chain that freezes the network or splits it.

leads.question: Why did 0xca52 addresses with byte 10 equal to 0x02 or 0xff revert under the Jenner override on bsc-dataseed1, when bsc v1.8.2 resolveCAS20Token returns no precompile for those ordinals and EVM.precompile treats the address as an ordinary account? Repeat the probe on dataseed1, 48 Club and reth-bsc with web3_clientVersion in the same batch, and compare it with the same call on an address of the 0x00 and 0x01 ordinals.
leads.why: If the deployed build routes addresses differently from its published tag, validators on different builds will disagree on CAS20 calls after 8 December. The same discrepancy may hide other routing differences that the battery cannot see because it calls only its own dispatcher.

leads.question: After Jenner, does the CAS20 Stablecoin variant (ordinal 0x01) have any path that changes a holder's balanceOf without a transfer by that holder, such as interest, rebase, a forced conversion or a mint to every holder, that an account with no role can trigger? Read cas20_token.go and the stablecoin variant file at v1.8.2.
leads.why: A balance change at the PoolManager that an ordinary account can trigger between its own sync and settle is booked as that account's payment (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A protocol-level token makes this a chain property rather than a token author's choice.

leads.question: On the C-Chain today, can any transaction an ordinary account sends write a multicoin balance into the PoolManager's account storage (AddBalanceMultiCoin through an atomic import, or the NativeAssetCall and NativeAssetBalance precompiles at 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000002 and 0x...0001)? Does setting the IsMultiCoin flag on the PoolManager account change what SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, SELFBALANCE or eth_getStorageAt return for it? Check with eth_call from the PoolManager address and in coreth source at the avalanchego 1.15.3 pin.
leads.why: The multicoin keys share the PoolManager's storage trie and are separated from EVM slots by one bit. A write path that skips the normalisation, or a flag that changes account handling, would let an ordinary account change PoolManager storage, which holds every pool's state.

leads.question: Does MegaETH use an OptimismPortal style bridge on Ethereum, and if so who can upgrade it, does mega-evm run deposit transactions without nonce and code checks as op-revm does, and does the portal alias contract senders? Read the portal proxy's implementation slot and verified source on Ethereum and the deposit handler in mega-evm v1.7.4.
leads.why: theme-inbox-deployed found on nine OP Stack chains that the portal upgrader can make a deposit carry the PoolManager as sender and move every pooled balance without unlock. MegaETH was left out of that check.

leads.question: Which Celo results of cycles 16 to 19 were not pinned to one client by web3_clientVersion in the same batch? For each, does the answer from forno's op-geth backend come from a head above block 75,046,581 and agree with celo-reth? Query eth_blockNumber and eth_getBlockByNumber for 75,046,581 in batches that also return the client string.
leads.why: A load balanced endpoint that mixes a stalled or diverged client with the producing client can make a fault on the producing client look absent.

leads.question: Does https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm answer eth_getStorageAt and eth_call at an old block number with the state of that block or with latest state? Test with a PoolManager slot0 slot of a pool whose price is known to have moved, and list the chain 999 clearances that used that endpoint for past blocks.
leads.why: If the endpoint ignores the block tag, replays and censuses that used it describe the wrong state, and the clearances built on them for the closed validator do not hold.

leads.question: For each network, what is the per-transaction gas cap a mined ordinary transaction has (EIP-7825 or the chain's own), and what gas does the heaviest liquidity removal, burn and take that an ordinary victim needs consume on a pool without a hook at the real PoolManager address? Measure with eth_estimateGas and compare with the cap, not with the eth_call limit.
leads.why: The claim that exits always fit in one transaction was measured under eth_call limits above the mined cap on at least the seven OP Stack chains. A removal that only fits in a simulated call would be a freeze for its owner.

leads.question: Can the compiler fix lists of the Go releases between go1.25.6 and go1.26.11 be read from go.dev/doc/devel/release or the go.googlesource.com mirror, and does any fix there name a miscompilation of a shape present in holiman/uint256 or in bor, BNB Chain geth or avalanchego core/vm?
leads.why: L-814 stalled on GitHub milestones only. These networks build their interpreters with these toolchains, and a miscompiled integer path changes pool math on every node of that build.

leads.question: For the OP Stack portal finding of theme-inbox-deployed, what delay separates a portal upgrade proposal from execution on each of the nine chains (Ethereum timelock, Security Council, or a Safe of EOAs as on X Layer), and is any upgrade queued now? Read the ProxyAdmin owner and its pending transactions on Ethereum.
leads.why: The finding is governance level. Its severity for deployment depends on how much warning LPs get, and X Layer's 2 of 3 Safe (F-026) may give none.

leads.question: Does any public artifact of mega-reth v2.3.1 (Docker image labels, a provider release note, a crates or container registry entry) name the mega-evm and revm revisions it pins, so the replica interpreter that serves eth_call can be tied to source?
leads.why: Every MegaETH opcode result speaks for the replica build, and the build changed this cycle to a revision no cycle has tied to source.

leads.question: On each network with protocol-implemented tokens at reserved addresses (Base B20 at 0xB200..., Tempo TIP-20 at 0x20c0..., Arc 0x3600..., HyperEVM system addresses, BNB Chain CAS20 after Jenner), does an eth_call state override that sets code at such an address take effect, or does the node keep routing to native code or disable the address as bsc's DisabledPrecompile does? List every earlier script or vector that placed a stand-in in such a range.
leads.why: bsc v1.8.2 core/vm/cas20.go documents that an override on a CAS20 address yields a precompile that reverts. A harness result in such a range then tests neither the stand-in nor the real token, and a clearance could rest on it.
